title: Hackers Hit Supermarket Fridges Across Europe
summary:
Hackers attacked supermarket fridges across Europe on Monday. Fridges and freezers in stores from Sweden to Belgium got too warm, so stores had to throw away spoiled food.

The attack hit dozens of stores. It hit supermarket groups Ahold Delhaize and Colruyt in Belgium and Luxembourg, and Swedish grocers ICA and Coop. At least one Ikea store was also affected.

At an ICA store in Stockholm, sales manager Engla Ingwall said the attack happened at 2 a.m. but was only noticed hours later. "Everything is destroyed," she said. "All our freezers reached 50 degrees [Celsius]."

No one has claimed responsibility for either attack. European authorities are worried about threats to important systems. Moscow has denied involvement.

Katrien Eggers, spokesperson for Belgium's Centre for Cybersecurity, said it is not known who is behind the attack, and it may never be determined. She said all computer systems can be vulnerable, and artificial intelligence can now be used to exploit these weaknesses.
why_it_matters: If fridges in shops stop working properly, the food your family buys could spoil, so keeping shop computers safe matters to everyone.

background_read: A hacker attack happens when someone breaks into a computer system to damage it or take control of it.
Many supermarket fridges are run by computers, so if hackers change their settings, the food inside can warm up and spoil.
That is why attacks on food stores worry people: one attack can spoil food in many shops at once.
